title: Natural Loose Parts
strapline: Big pinecones, smooth pebbles and wooden rings — real treasures from the natural world, safe to explore with hands and mouth.
intent: Babies and young toddlers explore natural materials with every sense — the weight of a pebble, the ridges of a pinecone, the cool of wood.
Children fill, empty, carry, hide and find, delighting in the movement of things.
Children make discoveries about how objects behave — they roll, they stack, they clunk, they fit inside.
Children build early concentration, choosing, mouthing, turning and studying one treasure at a time.
Children experience the natural world as fascinating and worth handling gently.
implementation: Choose only objects too large to be swallowed — big pinecones, large smooth pebbles, wooden curtain rings, fir cones, big shells — and check each one.
Stay close and attentive throughout: this is a supervised, sit-alongside experience, never left out unattended for this age.
Present the treasures in low open baskets so a crawling or sitting baby can reach in and choose.
Resist directing — let the baby mouth, bang, turn and drop, narrating quietly what they seem to notice.
Add containers — a metal tin, a wooden bowl — for the deep satisfaction of filling and emptying.
Wash and check the natural materials regularly, and rotate them with the seasons.
Follow the baby's fascination — if one pinecone holds them for ten minutes, that is the lesson.
key_questions: (For babies, wonder aloud rather than question) You're really studying that pinecone, aren't you?
In it goes... and out again — shall we fill it up once more?
That one is heavy and this one is light — can you feel it?
Which treasure will you choose next?
You made it clunk in the tin — did you hear that sound?

impact.text: Babies explore natural materials with all their senses, mouthing, turning and studying each treasure.
Children reach, grasp, transfer and release objects, exploring with hands and mouth.
Children fill, empty, hide and find, delighting in the movement of things.
Children explore how objects behave — rolling, stacking, dropping, posting.
Children concentrate deeply on a chosen treasure, showing sustained early attention.
Children notice 'more' and reach for another, and respond to a warm adult narrating alongside.

enhancements: Big pinecones, fir cones and large smooth pebbles, all checked for size.
Wooden curtain rings, bowls and big wooden beads to handle and clunk.
A metal tin and a basket for filling and emptying.
Large shells and pieces of driftwood, washed and smooth.
A low mirror behind the basket to double the treasures.
A soft blanket to sit and explore on within arm's reach of an adult.
Seasonal swaps — conkers (supervised, large), pine, blossom-time additions.

playing_exploring: Babies lead the exploration, choosing what to pick up and how to test it.
Every sense is at work — mouth, hands, ears and eyes all learning the object.
active_learning: A baby will return to a favourite treasure again and again, building early focus.
creating_thinking: Babies discover cause and effect — drop it and it clunks, tip it and it rolls.
They begin to expect what an object will do and test it once more.
